settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Organization, access and console preferences in one workspace.
settings.section.intelligence.hint: Advisory feeds and the daily re-check
settings.section.ai.hint: Providers, budget and the Shauron harness
appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.intro: Choose a contrast mode that stays calm through long investigations. System follows your device automatically.
language.title: Language
language.intro: The whole console follows this choice — sidebar, screens, forms and alerts. It is stored in this browser, not in the workspace.
language.addHint: Adding a language is a folder of JSON files: a new entry appears here without touching the screens.
language.reloadHint: Screens and labels switch immediately; open chapters and long-form text follow on the next load.
settings.org.name: Name
settings.org.errorNameShort: Organization name must be at least 2 characters.
settings.org.membersHint: Invite people, assign roles and manage seats.
settings.org.grantsHint: Review what scanner work is allowed to do.
settings.org.auditHint: Review recorded configuration and security actions.
settings.delivery.notificationsIntro: Notification preferences and delivery channels have their own operating screen, so alert history remains visible while you configure it.
settings.delivery.mailIntro: Invitations and email notification channels leave through this relay. Saving here overrides deployment variables.
settings.keys.title: Service identities
settings.keys.intro: Use service keys for automation. They are shown only once and revoked rather than deleted.
settings.keys.emptyHint: Create one only for a concrete automation need.
settings.keys.revokeBody: Clients using this key will stop working immediately. The last active key cannot be revoked.
settings.account.title: Account and sign-in
settings.account.localConnection: This browser controls the local console connection.
settings.account.mfaHint: Manage a second factor for your own account.
settings.account.orgSlugHint: Only when your email is in more than one organization.
settings.account.errorPasswordShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
security.title: My security
security.subtitle: Optional second factor for your own account — it is never enabled on your behalf
security.apiKey.title: Second factor needs a signed-in user
security.apiKey.emptyTitle: You are using an API key
security.apiKey.emptyHint: Multi-factor belongs to a person. Sign in with email and password (or SSO) to manage it.
security.mfa.title: Multi-factor authentication (TOTP)
security.mfa.intro: Works with any authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Aegis…). Enrolment is two steps: scan the secret, then prove a code from it.
security.mfa.errorCodeMismatch: That code did not match. Check the authenticator clock and try the next one.
security.enrol.intro: Scan with the authenticator, or type the secret. Nothing changes at login until you confirm a code.
security.recovery.intro: Save these now — they are shown once and each works a single time.
security.disable.codeLabel: Code or recovery code to turn it off
security.disable.errorCode: To turn the factor off you need a current code or a recovery code.
advisories.title: Advisory clock
advisories.intro: A bill of materials is a photograph: it says what the scanner knew the day it ran. This clock keeps asking after the scan, so a CVE published tomorrow still lands on the build you shipped today. It only adds — no import is rewritten and nothing is deleted.
advisories.autorun.before: This deployment runs the clock externally: nothing will happen on its own until the scheduler calls
advisories.runEnabled: Run the clock for this workspace
advisories.sources.osv.label: OSV.dev
advisories.sources.osv.hint: Re-asks the advisory database about every current build — this is what finds a CVE published after the scan.
advisories.sources.kev.label: CISA KEV
advisories.sources.kev.hint: Known exploited vulnerabilities. A fact, so it outranks any score.
advisories.sources.epss.label: EPSS
advisories.sources.epss.hint: Exploitation probability, refreshed for the advisories this workspace already holds.
advisories.sources.cpe.label: NVD — runtime CVEs
advisories.sources.cpe.hint: Node, Python, Go… matched by version range from NVD. OSV has no ecosystem for an interpreter, so this is the only source that answers for it.
advisories.interval.label: Every
advisories.interval.hint: hours. The platform checks on its own (every {minutes} min) and has this job decide whether it is due.
advisories.maxVersions.label: Builds per sweep
advisories.maxVersions.hint: The newest build of each component. Old builds keep their original evidence.
advisories.ecosystems.hint: Ecosystems to re-check — all of them when none is chosen.
advisories.savedNotice: Saved. The scheduler will use this on its next tick.
advisories.last.title: Last run
advisories.last.summary: {when} · {status} · {builds} builds re-checked · {created} new findings · {refreshed} refreshed · KEV {kev} · EPSS {epss}
advisories.last.next: Next run in {hours}h unless someone runs it now.
advisories.last.never: Never ran. Until it does, the console only knows what each scanner reported on the day it ran — a CVE published afterwards will not appear.
advisories.result.summary: This run: {status} · {builds} builds · {created} new · {refreshed} refreshed · {packages} packages asked
mail.error.hostRequired: A mail server name is required.
mail.error.testRecipient: Enter an address to receive the test.
mail.resetEnvironment: Configuration removed. The deployment environment takes over.
mail.resetOff: Configuration removed. Email delivery is off until one of the two is set.
mail.portHint: 587 with STARTTLS, 465 implicit TLS, 25 plain relay.
mail.passwordStoredPlaceholder: stored — leave blank to keep it
mail.passwordHint: Encrypted before it is stored; never shown again.
mail.starttlsHint: Most relays on port 587 require it; turn it off for a plain local relay.
mail.testHint: A configuration only counts once a server accepts a message.
runtimeSettings.title: Concurrency
runtimeSettings.intro.before: How many scans may run at once, and against whom. The platform enforces this when a worker claims a run: over the limit, the run stays
runtimeSettings.intro.after: with the reason — it is never silently dropped.
runtimeSettings.saved: saved — applies on the next claim, no restart
runtimeSettings.limits.title: Limits
runtimeSettings.waiting.title: Why a run is waiting
runtimeSettings.limit.perZone.label: concurrent runs per zone
runtimeSettings.limit.perZone.hint: subdomains of one domain count as one zone
runtimeSettings.limit.perOrg.label: concurrent runs per organization
runtimeSettings.limit.perOrg.hint: one tenant cannot drain the platform
runtimeSettings.limit.perWorker.label: runs per worker
runtimeSettings.limit.perWorker.hint: one run at a time keeps the trace readable
runtimeSettings.limit.queueCeiling.label: queue ceiling
runtimeSettings.limit.queueCeiling.hint: refuse new runs past this, with the reason
runtimeSettings.pool.minWorkers.label: minimum workers
runtimeSettings.pool.minWorkers.hint: the pool never drops below this — a queued run always has someone to run it
runtimeSettings.pool.maxWorkers.label: maximum workers
runtimeSettings.pool.maxWorkers.hint: the scaler never asks Swarm for more than this
runtimeSettings.pool.scaleDownAfter.hint: workers are cheap when idle and expensive to start
runtimeSettings.replicas.title: worker replicas now
runtimeSettings.preview.idle: nothing queued · up to {parallel} runs in parallel
runtimeSettings.preview.idleOne: nothing queued · up to {parallel} run in parallel
runtimeSettings.preview.note: The zone cap binds before the worker count does: {zone} at a time on any one domain, no matter how many workers are up. The pool floor is {min} — with zero workers a queue is indistinguishable from a broken scanner.
runtimeSettings.waiting.empty: nothing is waiting — every run in the queue has a worker free, or the queue is empty.
runtimeSettings.foot.after: , are read on every claim and audited on change — raising one is recorded like a grant, with who and when.
runtimeSettings.footnote: Barad-dûr runs in Docker, so the replica count is the deployment's business: this page reads the workers that register and never scales them. An app that could create containers would need the Docker socket, which is root on the host.
settings.section.mcp.hint: Connect an external agent: identity, address and catalogue.
mcp.title: Connect external agents over MCP
mcp.intro: The MCP server runs on the agent's side: this page gives it the identity, the address and the catalogue, which is everything it needs.
mcp.verdict: An MCP client acts as its own principal — the key you paste is yours, never a shared service identity.
mcp.identity.title: 1 · Identity
mcp.identity.intro: Issue one key per consumer, named after it. It is shown once.
mcp.identity.issue: Create a key for an agent
mcp.identity.shownOnce: Copy it now: it is never shown again.
mcp.identity.warning: A key is owner of the organization and bypasses the role checks. Revoke it from Service keys; the last active key cannot be revoked.
mcp.local.title: 2 · Local connection (stdio)
mcp.local.intro: For a client running on your machine: paste this block into its MCP configuration.
mcp.local.note: PYTHONPATH needs both repo folders; `python` is the interpreter that has the server's dependencies.
mcp.remote.title: 3 · Remote connection (HTTP)
mcp.remote.intro: For an agent that does not run on your machine: the server has to be hosted and reachable.
mcp.remote.note: The platform does not host the MCP server yet: that hosting is yours. The client points at {url} and sends the key in X-API-Key.
mcp.prompt.title: 4 · Instruction for the agent
mcp.prompt.intro: The server already sends these instructions when it connects, but many clients do not forward them to the model. Paste them as a system prompt if yours does not.
mcp.prompt.note: 'unknown' is not 'not affected'. That sentence is what stops an agent from inventing a verdict.
mcp.prompt.body: You are connected to Barad-dûr over MCP. {instructions} For anything else call `barad_tool` with {name, args}; if you do not know the name or the parameters, ask `barad_tools` first. Never invent hosts, versions or CVEs.
mcp.exposes.title: What it exposes
mcp.exposes.intro: {mcp} MCP tools over a catalogue of {n}: `{server}` imports it instead of copying it.
settings.section.integrations.hint: What the platform talks to: code host, Jira and mail — and where each setting comes from.
integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.intro: Everything this platform connects out to. Each block names its source: `saved` is a connection configured in the console, `environment` is this install's own variables. Settings here are read-only — the forms live in Connections and Delivery, so there is only one editor per row.
integrations.connections.title: Connections
integrations.connections.empty.hint: A code host and a ticket tracker are added during setup, or from Connections.
integrations.scm.title: Code host
integrations.jira.title: Jira
integrations.mail.title: Mail
integrations.mail.nopassword: A server is configured but no password: every send will be refused.
org.menu.title: Organisation
org.menu.new.hint: A separate estate: its own projects, scope and findings.
org.menu.key: Connected with an API key: a key belongs to one organisation. Sign in (Settings → account) to see and switch between the organisations you belong to.
